name: AI Data-Centre Liquid Cooling: Fluids, Hoses & Heat Exchangers
scope: Indian listed suppliers of coolants/dielectric fluids, liquid-cooling skids and hoses, and heat exchangers/cooling systems for AI data centres, and how much of the theme is already priced in.

summary.one_line: Most of the theme's stocks slid again this week, and only Blue Star is up over one month. Blue Star's Q2 FY27 call said it is not yet in liquid cooling and has no technology for it, even though it sizes India's liquid-cooling CDU market at about Rs 500 cr in FY27 and Rs 3,000 cr or more within about three years. CtrlS signed a Rs 10,000 cr MoU for a 150 MW AI data centre in Bihar, and Aeroflex is still the only listed name with large, disclosed liquid-cooling revenue.
key_points: Global growth forecasts differ widely. MarketsandMarkets puts data-centre liquid cooling at USD 4.07 bn in 2026, reaching USD 27.65 bn by 2033, a 31.5% CAGR (S24). IndexBox forecasts an 18.5% CAGR for direct-to-chip over 2026-2035, though the same page also gives a 12.0% baseline (S1). It forecasts 15.2% for immersion fluids (S2). It also says air cooling reaches its limit at 30 kW per rack, while AI racks exceed 100 kW (S1).

Mordor values India's data-centre cooling market at USD 2.99 bn in 2026 and forecasts USD 11.38 bn by 2032, a 24.86% CAGR. Liquid cooling is the fastest-growing segment at a 26.7% CAGR, while air cooling still holds 65.85% of the market in 2026 (S4).

New: according to a summary of Blue Star's Q2 FY27 call, the company sizes India's liquid-cooling CDU market at about Rs 500 cr in FY27, possibly Rs 3,000 cr or more in about three years. It says it is 'not a player' and has no technology yet, and that a technology tie-up or JV is still an open option. It expects Rs 10,000-12,500 cr of Indian data-centre orders to be finalised in FY27 (S21).

New: on 20 Nov, CtrlS signed an MoU with Bihar to invest Rs 10,000 cr in a 150 MW AI data centre near Patna, with operations targeted for 2029-30. The release says nothing about cooling (S19). JLL puts India's capacity at 1.6 GW in mid-2026 and expects 6 GW by 2029 (S3).

Aeroflex has raised its FY27 skid-revenue target to Rs 150-200 cr (S22). H1 FY27 skid revenue was Rs 82.42 cr: Rs 32.39 cr in Q1 and Rs 50.03 cr in Q2 (our sum, from S6). In India it supplies liquid cooling exclusively to one 'large US multinational' customer. Capacity is 12,000 skids a year, rising to 15,000 by December 2026 and 30,000 by March 2028 (S12).

KRN doubled Q2 FY27 revenue to Rs 319.14 cr, but its EBITDA margin fell to 15.27% from 19.90% and it gave no data-centre share (S20). Data centres were about 16% of FY26 revenue (S9). The stock is down 36.2% over three months (S16).

The fluids leg still discloses no data-centre revenue. Savita markets QuantiCool PG 25 (S8) and Apar markets Poweroil DC 10 (S11), but neither gives revenue figures. Navin Fluorine targets completion of its Chemours immersion-fluid project by end-Q3 FY27, with deliveries in Q4 FY27 (S25).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Aeroflex: it raised its FY27 skid-revenue target to Rs 150-200 cr (S22). Skid volumes rose from 1,040 units in Q1 to 1,475 in Q2 (S6). Its exclusivity covers only India, and talks with its existing customer about overseas supply are at an advanced stage (S12).

Local CDU and skid suppliers: Blue Star estimates the Indian liquid-cooling CDU market at about Rs 500 cr in FY27, possibly Rs 3,000 cr or more within about three years, and says it has no technology of its own yet (S21). That leaves room for partners and component makers.
KRN: revenue doubled in Q2, and new data-centre customers have started working with it (S20). It has passed Vertiv's quality audit (S9).

Navin Fluorine has purchase orders for Q4 FY27 delivery from its Chemours project (S25). Savita and Apar have data-centre fluids on the market with no disclosed revenue, an option the market is not yet paying for (S8, S11).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Aeroflex sells liquid cooling in India to one customer, under an exclusive arrangement. It does not bid directly to data-centre end users, and it does not disclose its order book (S12).
Global OEMs are localising: Vertiv makes its own SFN skids in India (S23) and supplies CDUs to Netweb (S14). Blue Star would need a technology tie-up to compete in liquid cooling (S21).
Aeroflex faces a Rs 41.76 cr tax demand for AY2018-19, which it is appealing (S5). Some of its Q2 profit growth came from a depreciation-method change worth Rs 8.41 cr (S6).
KRN's margin is falling as it scales, to a 15.27% EBITDA margin from 19.90% (S20). Its FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 113.80 cr (S9).
Air cooling still holds 65.85% of India's data-centre cooling market (S4), and new campuses such as CtrlS Bihar are years away from operation (S19).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Whether Aeroflex reaches 15,000 skids a year by December 2026 (S12), and its H2 skid revenue. The implied figure is Rs 68-118 cr: the FY27 target less H1's Rs 82.42 cr (our calculation, from S6 and S22).
A first overseas skid order for Aeroflex, or a second liquid-cooling customer (S12).
Whether Blue Star announces a liquid-cooling technology tie-up or JV (S21).

Completion of Navin's Chemours project by end-Q3 FY27 (S25). Whether KRN discloses a data-centre revenue share for FY27 (S9, S20). Whether Savita or Apar first disclose data-centre fluid revenue (S8, S11).

sections.title: Theme explainer: why AI is forcing liquid cooling

blocks.text: Liquid cooling removes heat with a fluid instead of air. In direct-to-chip (DTC) systems, a coolant runs through cold plates on the processors. The coolant is typically a glycol/water mix, such as Savita's QuantiCool PG 25 (S8). Coolant distribution units (CDUs), manifolds, SFN skids and hoses circulate it, and heat exchangers pass the heat to facility water (S23). In immersion cooling, servers sit in a dielectric (non-conductive) fluid. Examples are Apar's single-phase Poweroil DC 10 (S11) and the Chemours two-phase fluid that Navin Fluorine is preparing to make (S25). IndexBox says air cooling reaches its physical limit above 30 kW per rack and is no longer viable for hyperscalers above 50 kW, while AI/ML racks exceed 100 kW (S1).

blocks.text: The forecasts are not directly comparable. MarketsandMarkets' 31.5% covers the whole liquid-cooling market (S24), IndexBox's 18.5% covers direct-to-chip only (S1), and the two use different base years and horizons. IndexBox puts data centres at 45% of immersion-fluid demand in 2026, with the rest from EV batteries, HPC, transformers and crypto mining (S2). Indian fluid makers can therefore fill capacity from non-data-centre demand while data-centre orders build.

sections.title: India build-out, capex and local content

subsections.title: India data-centre pipeline and the liquid share

blocks.text: JLL's mid-year report estimates India's capacity at 1.6 GW in mid-2026 and forecasts 6 GW by 2029. H1 2026 absorption was 101 MW, 82% of it pre-committed hyperscale capacity (S3). New this week: on 20 Nov, CtrlS signed an MoU with the Bihar government for a Rs 10,000 cr, 150 MW 'hyperscale AI factory' on a 100-acre site near Patna, targeting commercial operations in 2029-30. The release says nothing about cooling (S19). On the demand side, Blue Star management expects about Rs 10,000-12,500 cr of Indian data-centre orders to be finalised in FY27 (S21). Vertiv calls CLDC Mumbai 01 in Airoli India's first direct-to-chip, high-density liquid-cooling deployment, supporting 30 MW of AI workloads (S23). For air versus liquid, Mordor gives air-based cooling 65.85% of the Indian market in 2026 and liquid a 26.7% CAGR over 2027-2032 (S4).

blocks.title: India data-centre capacity (JLL)
blocks.source: Source: JLL India Data Centre 2026 Mid-Year Report (S3)

blocks.text: No source states the liquid share of India's cooling market directly, and we have not derived one. The only confirmed DTC hyperscale deployment so far is the 30 MW at Airoli (S23), small against JLL's 1.6 GW base (S3). Blue Star's estimate of about Rs 500 cr for liquid-cooling CDUs in FY27 (S21) is also small against Mordor's USD 2.99 bn cooling market (S4).

items: Made in India by listed companies: Aeroflex skids and hoses (S6, S12), KRN coils (S9, S20), and Savita and Apar fluids (S8, S11). Navin's two-phase fluid has not yet been delivered (S25).
Global OEMs are localising the same items. Vertiv makes SFN skids in India (S23) and supplies CDUs and chillers for Netweb's systems (S14).
We found no Indian listed company with commercial CDU or cold-plate output. KRN's liquid-cooling products are in development (S20), and Blue Star says it does not yet have the technology (S21).

blocks.text: Aeroflex's Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 207.36 cr, against Rs 110.87 cr a year earlier. EBITDA rose 94.49% to Rs 50.34 cr and PAT rose 156.85% to Rs 36.56 cr, helped by an Rs 8.41 cr cut in depreciation from a method change. Skids brought in Rs 50.03 cr from 1,475 units (S6). Management said data centres are now the largest vertical and guided to FY30 revenue of close to Rs 1,500 cr at margins of about 25% (S22). It works exclusively with one customer for liquid cooling in India and does not disclose its order book (S12). KRN's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 109.86% to Rs 319.14 cr and PAT rose 100.3% to Rs 36.11 cr, but the EBITDA margin fell to 15.27% (S20). According to a summary of Blue Star's Q2 FY27 call, data-centre orders make up about Rs 2,000 cr of its roughly Rs 5,000 cr EMP order book. Management expects about Rs 4,000 cr of data-centre bookings in FY27 and data-centre revenue of about Rs 2,000 cr in FY27, rising to about Rs 4,000 cr by FY30. All of this is air-side and MEP work, since the company says it has no liquid-cooling technology yet (S21).

subsections.title: Fluids leg: products ready, revenue undisclosed

blocks.text: Savita's data-centre page lists QuantiCool PG 25 for direct liquid cooling but names no customers or revenue (S8). Its Phase 2 synthetic-ester plant at Mahad was commissioned on 28 Feb 2026, and the filing says esters suit data-centre cooling fluids (S10). Apar markets Poweroil DC 10 for single-phase immersion (S11) but discloses no revenue from it. Castrol India says data-centre cooling is not yet material (S13). Navin Fluorine's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 57% to Rs 1,190.7 cr. Management targets completion of the Chemours project by end-Q3 FY27, with purchase orders in place for delivery in Q4 FY27 (S25).

By market cap, quantified data-centre liquid-cooling revenue comes only from the small caps Aeroflex and KRN (S6, S9). Savita, also a small cap, has products but no disclosed revenue (S8). Among the mid caps, Blue Star has no liquid-cooling technology (S21), and Castrol and Netweb have products or adjacencies without disclosed liquid-cooling revenue (S13, S14). The large caps Apar and Navin have products but no disclosed revenue (S11, S25). This is a narrow, early niche, so the gap is real, not missed coverage. The Indian CDU makers we found, Refroid and KuhlTherm, are unlisted.

items: The hose and skid leg is re-rated but has cooled. Aeroflex is up 158.5% over one year and flat over three months (S7). KRN is de-rating, down 36.2% over three months (S16) even though Q2 revenue doubled (S20).
Blue Star is the only name up over one month (+14.0%) and three months (+18.5%) (S18). That rise rests on air-side data-centre orders, not liquid cooling, which it says it does not yet offer (S21).

The fluids leg's returns are not driven by data centres. Savita is up 41.6% over six months but down 15.6% over one month (S15). Apar is down 8.9% over one month (S17). Neither discloses data-centre fluid revenue (S8, S11).
Broker coverage is still thin. Coverage comes mainly from call summaries and retail and fintech media, such as DSIJ and Multibagg on Aeroflex (S6, S12, S22) and Trade Brains on Castrol (S13).

blocks.text: The Anand Rathi pages are internally inconsistent. Aeroflex, for example, shows a P/E of 69.84 in the fundamentals section and 58.72 in the FAQ, and the narrative returns differ from the tables. We use the table values and treat them as indicative (S7, S15, S16, S17, S18). For valuation, rely on the dashboard's screener.in feed.

items: Single-customer dependence: Aeroflex works exclusively with one customer for liquid cooling in India, does not bid to data-centre end users, and discloses neither its client count nor its order book (S12).
OEM localisation and the technology gap: Vertiv makes SFN skids at its own India facility (S23). Blue Star says it would need a technology arrangement or JV to enter liquid cooling (S21).
Utilisation: Aeroflex expects only 40-50% skid utilisation this year while it plans to double capacity (S12, S22).
Tax dispute: Aeroflex faces a Rs 41.76 cr income-tax demand for AY2018-19 and is appealing (S5).
Margins and working capital: KRN's Q2 EBITDA margin fell 4.63 points to 15.27% (S20), and its FY26 operating cash flow was -Rs 113.80 cr (S9).
Timing: air still holds 65.85% of India's data-centre cooling market (S4), and new AI campuses such as CtrlS Bihar target operations only in 2029-30 (S19).

companies.name: Aeroflex Industries Ltd
companies.role: Makes stainless-steel flexible hoses and liquid-cooling SFN skid assemblies. In India it supplies liquid cooling exclusively to one large US multinational customer (S6, S12).
companies.impact: Skids brought in Rs 50.03 cr in Q2 FY27 (S6), and the FY27 skid target is Rs 150-200 cr (S22). Capacity rises to 15,000 units by December 2026 and 30,000 by March 2028 (S12). It depends on one customer and faces a Rs 41.76 cr tax demand (S5, S12). The stock is up 158.5% over one year and flat over three months (S7).

companies.name: KRN Heat Exchanger and Refrigeration Ltd
companies.role: Makes fin-and-tube heat-exchanger coils for HVAC&R, including data-centre cooling. It has passed Vertiv's quality audit and is developing liquid-cooling products (S9, S20).
companies.impact: Q2 FY27 revenue doubled to Rs 319.14 cr, but the EBITDA margin fell to 15.27% and it disclosed no data-centre share (S20). Data centres were about 16% of FY26 revenue (S9). The stock is down 36.2% over three months (S16).

companies.name: Blue Star Ltd
companies.role: Executes data-centre MEP and cooling projects. Data-centre orders make up about Rs 2,000 cr of its roughly Rs 5,000 cr EMP order book (S21).
companies.impact: It guides to data-centre revenue of about Rs 2,000 cr in FY27, rising to about Rs 4,000 cr by FY30. It says it is not yet a liquid-cooling player and lacks the technology, and that a tie-up or JV is possible (S21). The stock is up 14.0% over one month (S18).

companies.name: Savita Oil Technologies Ltd
companies.role: Sells QuantiCool PG 25 coolant for direct liquid cooling, and commissioned Phase 2 of its Mahad synthetic-ester plant on 28 Feb 2026 (S8, S10).
companies.impact: It discloses no data-centre fluid revenue, so this remains an option the market is not pricing (S8). The stock is down 15.6% over one month (S15).

companies.name: Apar Industries Ltd
companies.role: Markets Poweroil DC 10, a single-phase immersion dielectric fluid, alongside data-centre cables (S11).
companies.impact: It discloses no data-centre fluid revenue. The stock is down 8.9% over one month and up 55.4% over one year (S11, S17).

companies.name: Navin Fluorine International Ltd
companies.role: Is building capacity to make Chemours' two-phase immersion-cooling fluid (S25).
companies.impact: Completion is targeted for end-Q3 FY27, with purchase orders for Q4 FY27 delivery, so there is no revenue yet (S25).

companies.name: Castrol India Ltd
companies.role: Has immersion and direct-to-chip coolants ready for India and in tests with OEMs (S13).
companies.impact: Management calls data-centre cooling not yet material, so there is no near-term earnings effect (S13).

companies.name: Netweb Technologies India Ltd
companies.role: Indian server OEM that builds direct-to-chip liquid-cooled GPU systems with Vertiv's CDUs and chillers (S14).
companies.impact: A downstream adjacency: it pulls liquid-cooling content through its systems rather than making fluids or hardware (S14).

method:
W48 refresh of the W47 edition, researched on 2026-11-23 with web search and page fetches.

New this week:
- CtrlS's 20 Nov press release on its 150 MW Bihar MoU (S19).
- A summary of Blue Star's Q2 FY27 call (S21). It replaces the October Trade Brains roundup that W47 cited for a Blue Star CDU 'in development'. The call summary says Blue Star has no liquid-cooling technology and would need a tie-up or JV. It is a third-party paraphrase, not a transcript, so we treat it as indicative.
- The MarketsandMarkets liquid-cooling forecast (S24). The page returned HTTP 403, so its figures are taken from the search-result listing of the press release.

Re-verified: all five Anand Rathi quote pages were re-opened on 23 Nov, with tables updated 20 Nov, and every return and market-cap figure was updated. KRN's three-month return worsened to -36.2%, and Blue Star turned positive.

Dropped:
- The Univest Savita Q2 note and the FPJ note on Aeroflex's funding mix (the dashboard carries the financials).
- The Trade Brains supplier roundup.

Read but not cited:
- Apar's Q2 FY27 call summary (CompoundingAI). It shows a data-centre cable order book of about Rs 1,000 cr and no mention of Poweroil.
- The Aeroflex CFO change, effective 28 Nov 2026 (Arthneeti).
- A BPCL-Refroid indigenous data-centre coolant, launched Feb 2025 with no volumes or revenue. It was too thin to qualify BPCL.

Screened but excluded: Refroid and KuhlTherm (unlisted) and Schneider/Motivair (foreign parent). Voltas and Gulf Oil have no confirmed current liquid-cooling products.

Carried over without re-opening: S1-S6, S8-S14, S20, S22, S23, S25.

Our calculations: Aeroflex's H1 skid revenue, its skid share of Q2 revenue, and its implied H2 skid revenue (from S6 and S22).

No ratings or price targets.
